Rashi on Temurah 2b:10:1.hebrew: בכולן רואה אני להחמיר - דלא נהנין ומועלין, וחייבין עליהן משום פגול, נותר וטמא כשאר קדשים — חוץ מן הנסכים, דודאי אין מביאין:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:10:1.english: With regard to all of them I see [fit] to be stringent - That one may not derive benefit [from them], and one is liable for misuse [if one does]; and one is liable for them on account of piggul, notar, and ritual impurity, like other consecrated offerings — except for libations, which they certainly do not bring.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:10:2.hebrew: בד"א - לעיל קמהדר, ואמילתיה דת"ק. וה"ק: בד"א דקאמר תנא קמא אינו מועלין — בקדשי מזבח של עובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:10:2.english: In what case is this statement said - It refers back to earlier, to the statement of the first Tanna, and this is what it is saying: In what case is this statement said, that the first Tanna said one is not liable for misuse? With regard to [offerings] consecrated for the altar of a gentile.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:10:3.hebrew: אבל בקדשי בדק הבית - שהקדישו עובד כוכבים, מועלין. ובמסכת זבחים מפרש טעמא בפ' ב"ש (זבחים דף מה.), ואית דגרסי לה נמי לקמן הכא בתמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:10:3.english: But with regard to [items] consecrated for Temple maintenance - that a gentile consecrated [them], [the laws of] misuse apply [to them]. And in tractate Zevachim the reason is explained in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (Zevachim 45a), and some have the reading [of it] later on here in Temurah as well.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:10:4.hebrew: קתני מיהא - דקדשי עובדי כוכבים אינן עושין תמורה, ותיפשוט מהא:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:10:4.english: In any event, it teaches - That consecrated animals of gentiles do not effect a substitution, and let [the question] be resolved from this:

Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:1.hebrew: אמר לו בהקדש עובדי כוכבים - כלומר, אי משום הא לא איריא, דמהכא ליכא למיפשט כלל, דהיכא דהקדיש עובד כוכבים להתכפר עובד כוכבים — שהפרישו לצורך כפרת עצמו:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:1.english: He said to him: With regard to consecration by gentiles - That is to say: If [it is] because of that, it is no proof, for from here it cannot be resolved at all, as [the case] where a gentile consecrated [an offering] for a gentile to achieve atonement [means] that he separated it for his own atonement.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:2.hebrew: לא קמיבעיא לי - דאין הקדשו עושה תמורה, הואיל ולא אתי לכלל עונשין:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:2.english: I do not raise a dilemma - For his consecrated [animal] does not effect substitution, since he is not subject to punishments.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:3.hebrew: ומתכפר ישראל - שהפרישו עובד כוכבים לצורך ישראל, שיתכפר בו ישראל:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:3.english: And an Israelite achieves atonement - Where a gentile designated it for the sake of an Israelite, so that an Israelite would achieve atonement with it.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:4.hebrew: בתר מקדיש אזלינן - והמקדיש הוי עובד כוכבים, דלא אתי לכלל עונשין, ואינו עושה תמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:4.english: Do we follow the one who consecrated - And the one who consecrated is a gentile, who does not come within the category of punishments and [therefore] does not effect substitution.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:5.hebrew: או בתר מתכפר - שהוא ישראל, ואיתיה בכלל מלקות:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:11:5.english: Or [do we follow] the one achieving atonement - Who is an Israelite, and is subject to lashes.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:12:1.english: This is the reading: “Resolve it from that which Rabbi Abbahu said” - [As stated] below.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:12:2.hebrew:
המקדיש מוסיף חומש - שאם רוצה לפדות הקדשו, כגון שנפל בו מום — יכול לפדותו, ומוסיף חומש; אבל מימר אינו מוסיף חומש, דכתיב: "אם המקדיש וגו'" (ויקרא כז) — על הקדש ראשון אתה מוסיף חומש, ולא על הקדש שני, כגון תמורה.
ע"א: שאם הקדיש בית או שדה, ואתו בעלים לפדותו — לא פרקי בלא חומש, דכתיב (שם): "ואם המקדיש יגאל ויסף חמישיתו", אבל אם גאלו אחר — לא חייביה רחמנא ליתן חומש:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:12:2.english:
The one who consecrates adds a fifth - That if he wishes to redeem his consecrated [animal], for example, if a blemish befell it — he may redeem it, and he adds a fifth; but one who substitutes [when redeeming the substitute] does not add a fifth, as it is written: “If the one who consecrates, etc.” (Leviticus 27) — you add a fifth upon a primary consecration, but not upon a secondary consecration, such as a substitute.
Another explanation: That if one consecrated a house or a field, and the owner comes to redeem it, he does not redeem [it] without a fifth, as it is written (ibid.): “And if the one who consecrates [it] shall redeem [it], he shall add its fifth”; but if another [person] redeemed it, the Merciful One did not obligate him to give a fifth.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:12:3.hebrew: ומתכפר עושה תמורה - שאם הפריש ישראל קרבן כדי שיתכפר בו חבירו ישראל, ואמר המתכפר "זו תחת זו" — תמורתו תמורה, ולוקה, דכיון שהופרש לצורכו, קרינא ביה "קרבנו", דבתר המתכפר אזלינן. ותיפשוט מהא:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:12:3.english: And the one achieving atonement effects substitution - That if an Israelite set aside an offering so that his fellow Israelite would achieve atonement with it, and the one achieving atonement said, “This [animal is] in place of that [one],” his substitution takes effect, and he incurs lashes, for since it was set aside for his sake, we read concerning it “his offering,” as we follow the one achieving atonement. And let [the dilemma] be resolved from this.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:12:4.english: And one who separates teruma - From his own produce for his fellow's untithed produce, to exempt him from the tithes.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:1:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: ״ויליף סוף הקדש מתחלת הקדש כו'״:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:1:1.english: This is the reading: “And he derives the end of consecration from the beginning of consecration, etc.”

Rashi on Temurah 2b:2:1.hebrew: את האשה - שתמורתה תמורה, ולקיא משום לאו דלא ימיר:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:2:1.english: A woman - That her substitution takes effect, and she receives lashes on account of the negative prohibition of “He shall not substitute.”

Rashi on Temurah 2b:2:2.hebrew: אלא בלשון זכר דכתיב לא יחליפנו - דהיינו לשון זכר, ולא כתיב לא תחליפנו, דהוי לשון נקבה:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:2:2.english: Only in the masculine, as it is written: “He shall not exchange it” - That is, the masculine form, and it is not written: “She shall not exchange it,” which would be the feminine form.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:2:3.hebrew: מה סופנו לרבות כו' - כלומר, מהיכן נלמוד שסופנו לרבות את האשה:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:2:3.english: What is our end to include, etc. - That is to say, from where do we learn that we ultimately include a woman?

Rashi on Temurah 2b:2:4.english: The verse states: “And if he shall at all substitute” - Since the verse wrote [it] twice.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:3:1.hebrew: ולר' מאיר - דאיצטריך ליה ואם המר ימיר לרבות יורש, אשה מנא ליה:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:3:1.english: And according to Rabbi Meir - Since he required “And if he shall at all substitute” to include an heir, from where does he derive [the inclusion of] a woman?

Rashi on Temurah 2b:3:2.hebrew: נפקא ליה מוי"ו - מדמצי למכתב אם המר ימיר, וכתיב ואם:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:3:2.english: He derives it from the [letter] vav - Since [the verse] could have written: “If he shall at all substitute,” and it is written: “And if.”

Rashi on Temurah 2b:4:1.hebrew: לא לקיא - דאם המירה, תמורתה אינה תמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:4:1.english: She is not flogged - For if she substituted, her substitution is not a [valid] substitution.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:5:1.hebrew: ומשני, ה"ג: הני מילי לאו שיש בו מעשה - בהני עונשין שוין זה לזה, דכתיב אשר יעשו, דמשמע עונשין שיש בהן מעשה, כגון חילול שבת ושאר איסורים שיש בהן מעשה. אבל לאו שאין בו מעשה, כגון תמורה, דבדיבורא תליא מילתא — אימא לא תילקי, קמ"ל:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:5:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers, this is the reading: This applies to a negative commandment that involves an action - In these [cases], they are equal to one another in punishment, as it is written: “Which they shall commit,” which implies punishments that involve an action, such as desecration of Shabbat and other prohibitions that involve an action. But [as for] a negative commandment that does not involve an action, such as substitution, where the matter depends on speech — [lest you] say that she is not flogged, [the verse] teaches us [that she is liable].

Rashi on Temurah 2b:5:2.hebrew: ל"א כתוב בספרים הני מילי עונש דשוה בין ביחיד בין בצבור - בהאי עונש הוא דהושוו זה לזה, אבל הכא בתמורה, אין צבור עושין תמורה, כדאמרינן באידך פירקין (דף יג.), וקא מפיק ליה ממעשר:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:5:2.english: Another version is written in the books: “This applies to a punishment that applies equally to an individual and to the public” - It is with regard to this punishment that they were equated to one another [i.e., woman to man]; but here regarding substitution, the public does not effect substitution, as we say in the other chapter (folio 13a), and it derives this from [animal] tithe.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:6:1.hebrew: שלא הגיע לעונת נדרים - כגון דהוי פחות מי"ב שנה, דהכי אמרינן במסכת נזיר (דף סב.): איש כי יפליא — מה ת"ל? דהכי מצי למכתב: איש כי ידור נדר, אלא לרבות מופלא הסמוך לאיש, כגון בן י"ב שנה, דכיון שיודע להפלות לשם מי נדר ולשם מי הקדיש — נדרו נדר והקדשו הקדש. פחות מכן — אפי' ידע למי נדר ולמי הקדיש, אין בדבריו כלום. יותר על כן, כגון בן י"ג שנה — אע"פ שאינו יודע לשם מי הפליא, הוו מעשיו מעשה:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:6:1.english: [One] who has not reached the age of vows - For example, where he is less than twelve years [old], for so we say in Tractate Nazir (62a): 'When a man clearly articulates [a vow]' — what does the verse teach? For it could have written: 'When a man vows a vow.' Rather, [it comes] to include a *mufla hasamukh le'ish* [a discerning minor nearing adulthood], such as one who is twelve years old, for since he knows to clearly articulate for Whose sake he vowed and for Whose sake he consecrated, his vow is a vow and his consecration is a consecration. [At an age] less than this, even if he knew to Whom he vowed and to Whom he consecrated, his words are nothing. More than this, such as one who is thirteen years old, even though he does not know for Whose sake he clearly articulated [it], his actions are valid.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:6:2.english: He cannot consecrate - As I explained above, that there is nothing to his words.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:6:3.hebrew: אמורי מימר - בתמיה, כי היכי דלילקי:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:6:3.english: Can he effect substitution - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question: [Would he effect substitution] so that he would be flogged?!

Rashi on Temurah 2b:6:4.hebrew: שהגיע לעונת נדרים - דהוי בן י"ב שנה, דקאמרינן התם דנדריו נבדקין, ואם יודע לשם מי הפליא — הוו מעשיו מעשה, ואי לא — לא:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:6:4.english: Who has reached the age of vows - That he is twelve years old, as we say there that his vows are examined; and if he knows to Whom he dedicated [the vow], his actions are [effective] actions, and if not, [they are] not.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:7:1.english: Since he is not subject to punishment - Until thirteen years [of age].

Rashi on Temurah 2b:7:2.hebrew: לא מיתפיס - בה תמורה, דכתיב: "לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו והיה הוא ותמורתו". כלומר, מאן דאיתיה בכלל "לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר" — כגון בר עונשין — איתיה נמי בכלל "והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש", דמתפיס בתמורה; לאפוקי קטן, דלאו בר עונשין הוא:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:7:2.english: [Does] not take effect - Substitution [does not take effect] upon it, as it is written: “He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it… and it and its substitute [shall be holy]” (Leviticus 27:10). That is to say: Whoever is included in “He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it” — such as one who is subject to punishment — is also included in “then it and its substitute shall be holy,” so that he can effect substitution; to exclude a minor, who is not subject to punishment.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:8:1.hebrew: ואפילו אם תמצא לומר קטן עביד תמורה כו' - רבותא אתא לאשמועינן, ולא משום דאיתיה הכי:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:8:1.english: And even if you say that a minor can effect substitution, etc. - It comes to teach us a greater novelty, and not because it is actually so.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:8:2.hebrew: מדאקדושי מקדיש - דהא מרבינן במנחות (דף עג:): ״איש איש מבני ישראל אשר יקריב קרבנו״, ואמרינן: מה ת"ל ״איש איש״? לרבות עובדי כוכבים, שנודרין נדרים ונדבות כישראל:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:8:2.english: From [the fact] that he consecrates - For we derive in Menachot (73b): “Any man [ish ish] of the children of Israel who brings his offering”, and we say: What does the verse teach by [stating] “ish ish”? To include gentiles, that they may take vows [to bring] vow offerings and gift offerings like an Israelite.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:8:3.hebrew: דלא אתי לכלל עונשין - דעובד כוכבים לא לקי לעולם, אבל קטן אתי לכלל עונשין כשהוא בן י"ג שנה ויום אחד:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:8:3.english: Since he will not come into the category of punishments - For a gentile never receives lashes, but a minor will come into the category of punishments when he is thirteen years and one day old.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:9:1.hebrew: לא נהנין ולא מועלין - שאם נהנה מהן, לא מייתי קרבן מעילה, דלא דיינינן ליה כשאר קדשים שהנהנה מהן מעל, משום דלא אסור בהנאה אלא מדרבנן, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:9:1.english: [One] may not derive benefit, nor is [one] liable for misuse - That if one derived benefit from them, he does not bring an offering for misuse, for we do not judge it like other consecrated offerings, [where] one who derives benefit from them has committed misuse, because it is forbidden to derive benefit [from it] only rabbinically, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:9:2.english: And one is not liable on their account, etc. - As [the Gemara] concludes below.

Rashi on Temurah 2b:9:3.hebrew: ואין מביאין כו' — ה"ג: ואין מביאין נסכים, ול"ג: עליהן - והכי פירושא: דאין מביאין נסכים של עובדי כוכבים בפני עצמן, כישראל שמתנדב נסכין בפני עצמן. אבל בהדי קרבנו מביאין, כדאמרינן במסכת שקלים (פ"ז מ"ו) שזו אחת מן התקנות שתיקנו ב"ד: דעובד כוכבים ששילח עולתו ודמי נסכיהן ממדינת הים — מקבלין הימנו. אבל קרבנו ודאי טעון נסכים, דבהדי קרבנו מביא נסכים:
Rashi on Temurah 2b:9:3.english: “And one does not bring, etc.” — this is the reading: “And one does not bring libations,” and we do not read: “for them” - And this is the explanation: That one does not bring libations of gentiles by themselves, like an Israelite who volunteers libations by themselves. However, together with his offering, one does bring [them], as we say in Tractate Shekalim (7:6), that this is one of the ordinances that the court instituted: that a gentile who sent his burnt-offering and the money for their libations from overseas — they accept [them] from him. However, his offering certainly requires libations, for together with his offering he brings libations.

Tosafot on Temurah 2b:10:1.hebrew: במה דברים אמורים בקדשי מזבח אבל בקדשי בדק הבית מועלין - פרש"י דאתאן לר"ש. ור"י פירש דמסקנא דמילתא דר' יוסי, וה"ק: רבי יוסי אומר "בכולן אני רואה להחמיר", והא דקאמר ר"ש "אין מועלין בהן" — בד"א בקדשי מזבח כו'. ובתוספתא משמע כפרש"י, דאיתא בהדיא: "אבל בקדשי בדק הבית מודה רבי שמעון":
Tosafot on Temurah 2b:10:1.english: "In what case is this statement said? With regard to consecrations for the altar, but with regard to consecrations for Temple maintenance, one is liable for misuse" - Rashi explained that we have returned to [the statement of] Rabbi Shimon. And the Ri explained that [this clause] is the conclusion of Rabbi Yosei's statement, and this is what it means: Rabbi Yosei says, "With regard to all of them I see fit to be stringent; and as for that which Rabbi Shimon said, 'One is not liable for misuse of them' — in what case is this statement said? With regard to consecrations for the altar, etc." And in the Tosefta, it implies in accordance with Rashi's explanation, as it is stated explicitly: "However, with regard to consecrations for Temple maintenance, Rabbi Shimon concedes [that one is liable for misuse]."

Tosafot on Temurah 2b:10:2.hebrew: קתני מיהת אין עושין תמורה - וא"ת: ודילמא לרבי יוסי קבעי, דאמר בכולן להחמיר? וי"ל: דניחא ליה לאוקומי הבעיא אף לר"ש. עי"ל: דע"כ דלרבי יוסי לא אפשר לאוקומי הבעיא; דכיון דאית ליה דעושין תמורה — דאפילו את"ל דהיינו על ידי ישראל, ומבעיא ליה לרמי בר חמא אם העובד כוכבים עצמו אפשר לעשותה, הא לא מצית אמרת! דע"כ אם ישראל מתפיסה, צריך שיאמר העובד כוכבים: "כל הרוצה להמיר יבא וימיר", ואם העובד כוכבים עצמו אין עושה תמורה, היאך אפשר לעשות עולה:
Tosafot on Temurah 2b:10:2.english: "In any event, it teaches: They do not effect substitution" - And if you say: But perhaps [Rami bar Ḥama] was asking according to Rabbi Yosei, who said [that he sees fit] to be stringent with regard to all of them? And one can say: It was preferable to him [= Rava] to establish the dilemma [as arising] even according to Rabbi Shimon. Furthermore, one can say: Perforce, it is not possible to establish the dilemma according to Rabbi Yosei; for since he holds that they do effect substitution — for even if you were to say that this is [only] by means of a Jew, and Rami bar Ḥama's dilemma was whether the gentile himself can perform it — you cannot say this! For perforce, if a Jew designates it [as a substitute], the gentile must say: "Whoever wishes to substitute, let him come and substitute," and if the gentile himself cannot effect substitution, how is it possible to make [the replacement animal an] olah?

Tosafot on Temurah 2b:9:1.hebrew: ואין מביאין נסכים - פרש"י: ואין מביאין של עובד כוכבים בפני עצמן, כישראל שמתנדבין נסכים בפני עצמן; אבל בהדי קרבנו מביאין, כדאמר במסכת שקלים (דף יא עמוד ד), דזה אחת מן התקנות שהתקינו ב"ד: דעובד כוכבים שמשלח עולתו ודמי נסכו ממדינת הים — שמקבלין ממנו. אבל ודאי קרבנו טעון נסכים — דבהדי קרבנו (טעון נסכים ו) מביאין נסכים משל צבור:
Tosafot on Temurah 2b:9:1.english: "And one does not bring libations" - Rashi explained: And [this means that] one does not bring [the libations] of a gentile on their own, like Israelites who volunteer libations on their own; but together with his sacrifice they do bring [them], as it says in tractate Shekalim (folio 11, column 4), that this is one of the enactments that the court instituted: that with regard to a gentile who sends his burnt offering and the money for his libations from overseas, they accept [them] from him. However, his sacrifice definitely requires libations — for together with his sacrifice ([it requires libations, and]) they bring libations from communal funds.
